# Pokémon Survivors

> A free, unofficial Vampire Survivors-style Pokémon fan game (action roguelite / bullet heaven) that runs in the browser and on phones, with no download, no sign-up, no ads and no purchases. Available in English, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. Made by Pedro Barretto; open source on GitHub.

Pick one of 27 starter Pokémon from every region (Kanto to Paldea), walk around and let it attack on its own. Survive 15 minutes of wild Pokémon hordes, collect experience, learn moves, equip held items and evolve mid-run, then face Mewtwo. After the victory you can keep going in an endless mode, where the horde keeps scaling and Arceus hunts you as the reaper.

- 27 starters, each with its full 3-stage evolution line, stats, signature move and learnset
- Eggs: bosses, locked chests and rifts sometimes drop an egg; it waits in a 3-slot incubator and hatches with the steps walked in runs, unlocking one of 54 more playable families (every type and generation, e.g. Pichu, Eevee, Gastly, Magikarp, Riolu, Gible, Bagon, Deino, Dreepy). 1% of hatchlings are shiny for good; duplicates become Poké Dollars. A 55th family, Munchlax → Snorlax, only hatches from the Friendship Egg (82 playable Pokémon in all)
- Invites and Mystery Gifts: every shared link carries the player's handle; a friend who signs up through it gets a Friendship Egg, and the inviter gets gifts once the friend has finished 3 runs (1 friend: a Friendship Egg; 3: the Ambassador title and an exclusive card frame; 5: an Ultra rare egg; 10: a shiny Dratini). The home screen's Invite friends card shows the link, the reward ladder and each invited friend's progress. Public profiles show how many friends a player brought
- 196 moves and 32 held items. Every family has its own signature move (Brave Bird, Weather Ball, Spore, Fiery Dance, Gigaton Hammer, Moonblast…) and a learnset that grows at each evolution, with more moves than the 6 slots, so runs build differently. A maxed regular move plus the right item evolves (Ember + Charcoal → Flamethrower; 48 move evolutions, 7 type items for Fighting, Steel, Ghost, Dark, Psychic, Ground and Fairy), and evolved moves keep leveling up to Lv 5
- Level-up choices: every base move forks into two paths at Lv 4 and Lv 7 that change how it plays (bounce, explode, trail, echo…); cards roll a rarity (rare: +2 levels; shiny, 1 in 64: a free pick); a Forget button bans an offer for the rest of the run (charges from the Escape Rope, bosses and evolutions); and each run opens with a draft for the 2nd move
- 91 Abilities, one picked out of 3 at the first evolution (the third is the Hidden Ability), and branching evolutions: Eevee picks among its 8 eeveelutions (the weather and place favor one), Kirlia picks Gardevoir or Gallade, and Snorunt, Poliwhirl, Scyther and Charcadet branch too, each form with its own type, special, moves and Abilities
- Moves from outside the learnset: every beaten wave boss drops a TM (Rock Slide, Yawn, Ice Beam, Discharge, Heat Wave, Psystrike…), a Move Tutor tent teaches moves that suit the player's type but sit outside its learnset, and each rift legendary or final mythical offers its own legendary move (Whirlwind, Sacred Fire, Origin Pulse, Roar of Time, Wish…; one per run). With 6 moves, learning asks which one to forget
- Duo moves: two maxed moves whose types form a recipe fuse into Fire Pledge, Water Pledge, Grass Pledge, Fusion Flare, Fusion Bolt, Ion Deluge, Freeze-Dry or Nightmare (one per run). Locked chests may hide a cursed item (Life Orb, Choice Band, Flame Orb, Iron Ball): strong, at a price, take it or leave it
- Type matchups, burn, poison, paralysis, slow, sleep, freeze, confusion, marks, Leech Seed-style seeds and weaken, and a manual special attack for each of the 18 types that grows stronger at the final evolution (Blast Burn, Hydro Cannon, Frenzy Plant, Bolt Strike, Draco Meteor, Astral Barrage, Precipice Blades, Aeroblast and more). Agile lines (Treecko, Sprigatito, Riolu, Gible, Starly, Honedge) get a chain dash instead: a lunge into the nearest foe that can jump again to the next one right after a hit; Aegislash gets Stance Change, swapping between Shield Forme (takes less damage) and Blade Forme (hits harder)
- 415 wild Pokémon from all 9 generations (Dragon types included), with every non-legendary Kanto, Johto and Hoenn species (but Unown and Castform), in 5 tiers by base stat total; every run draws its own cast (basic Pokémon early, evolved ones late), weighted towards the types of each biome
- Legendary bosses with telegraphed attacks: Onix, Snorlax, a legendary trio drawn per run for the 7:00, 9:30 and 12:00 slots (Kanto birds Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres; Johto beasts Raikou, Entei and Suicune; or Hoenn Regis Regirock, Regice and Registeel; each slot has the same stats whichever trio comes) and Mewtwo, sometimes joined by a rare mythical (Mew, Celebi or Jirachi, 10%). Each one switches between close and ranged attacks and enrages under half HP, the horde thins for the first minute of each boss, and each boss has until the next one arrives, then it flees; Mewtwo, the finale, blasts the horde away and thins it further while it stands. Bosses aim at the path the player is taking, leap at a player who keeps away, unlock a new attack when enraged and get an extra one on Nightmare; on Hard and Nightmare Mewtwo has a second phase
- Elites and runners: when the horde nearly fills, new enemies come in as tougher elites (except during the Mewtwo duel), and one new species each stage runs and aims where the player is heading. Another species per stage spits: it keeps its distance and fires slow, telegraphed shots flavored by its type (fire, water, poison puddles, electric, grass) that pass through the player's aura
- Alpha Pokémon: from about 4:00, oversized red-glowing members of the stage's top tier join the horde; they ignore knockback and charge along a red lane they aim first (on Nightmare the charge ends in a shockwave and they enrage). Beating one gives EXP, ₽ and the Alpha's prize, a level-up of rare cards; the Alpha Hunter title comes with 100 of them
- Five biomes per run (Route 1, Viridian Forest, Mt. Moon, Mt. Silver, Lavender Tower), each with its own music, and weather that shifts type matchups for everyone: harsh sunlight, rain, sandstorm, snow and fog
- Special enemies with behavior traits, at most one per stage of a run: Chansey heals the horde, Bronzor and Bronzong shield it, Nidoqueen summons Nidoran, Voltorb, Electrode and Drifloon explode, Magnemite and Vikavolt fire telegraphed beams and Hitmonlee and Lokix leap over the horde
- Legendary rifts: three optional portals per run to arenas with Lugia, Ho-Oh, Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza, Dialga, Latias, Latios and Deoxys (possibly shiny), each with its own shape and terrain (shallow water, pillars, a rising tide, lava rivers, a crumbling edge, an island ringed by surf, a meteor in space), for big rewards
- Mega Evolution: the first rift legendary beaten with a Mega line drops its Mega Stone; at the final evolution a MEGA button (E key, gamepad Y) Mega Evolves for 20 s with a 60 s recharge. 38 Megas across 33 lines, each with its own stats, special and ability: Mega Venusaur, Mega Charizard X (Dragon Flare, a blue dragon-fire dash) and Y (Drought: harsh sunlight), Mega Blastoise, Mega Raichu X and Y, Mega Alakazam (Trace: every special also fires two of your moves), Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag: foes nearby are slowed), Mega Dragonite, Mega Meganium, Mega Feraligatr, Mega Tyranitar (Sand Stream: a sandstorm it is immune to), Mega Sceptile, Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert (Swift Swim: rain), Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate, Moonblast), Mega Gallade (Inner Focus: a 6-jump chain dash that bursts Aura Spheres), Mega Pidgeot (No Guard, Air Slash), Mega Gyarados, Mega Ampharos, Mega Scizor (Technician, Bullet Punch chain dash), Mega Houndoom, Mega Aggron (Filter), Mega Manectric (Intimidate: foes nearby are slowed), Mega Altaria (Pixilate), Mega Banette (Prankster), Mega Glalie (Refrigerate), Mega Salamence (Aerilate), Mega Metagross, Mega Staraptor, Mega Garchomp and Mega Garchomp Z, Mega Lucario (Adaptability, a 6-jump chain dash bursting Aura Spheres) and Mega Lucario Z, Mega Emboar, Mega Chesnaught, Mega Delphox and Mega Greninja. A line with two Megas gets both stones and keeps the one it picks up
- Endless mode after Mewtwo, scored by time survived, with Arceus as a hunting reaper that can be defeated
- Three difficulty levels, all open from the start: Normal, Hard (faster, denser hordes that hit harder) and Nightmare (brutal, fast and dense hordes and half of every heal). Standing still doesn't work: late hordes resist knockback and hit harder, armor takes off at most half of a hit, a hidden pressure director sends faster and closer spawns to a player who isn't getting hurt, and the map itself strikes where the player stands (Thunder in the rain, hail in the snow, Rock Slide in a sandstorm, Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes), always telegraphed on the ground
- Rankings by time survived, one per difficulty, for today, this week and all time (days and weeks follow Brasília time), filterable by starter and by friends (one-way follows). Signed-in players get a public profile at /?u=handle with their title, records, Pokédex progress and recent runs. A ranked run shows on the boards as soon as it ends, within what a start token's wall clock allows; the server re-simulates the replays of the runs at the top (the simulation is deterministic across browsers) and takes off any that don't end where they said
- Shiny wild Pokémon and shiny starters; Poké Dollars and permanent upgrades in the Poké Mart (the Shiny Charm takes wild shiny odds from 1/450 to 1/225)
- Daily mass outbreak: one wild species per day (Brasília time), the same for everyone, is the most common Pokémon of every run that day, so its shiny shows up about twice a run; a daily mission asks to defeat it
- Daily Challenge: one run per day (Brasília time) that is the same for everyone, drawn from the date: seed, Pokémon (any playable one, egg families not yet hatched included) and difficulty, with no Poké Mart upgrades, Lure, Incense or Shiny Charm, and the day's outbreak on. Only each player's first finished run counts on the challenge board (today and yesterday), the rest are practice; the server checks the run is the day's challenge and re-simulates it. After the day closes, everyone on the board gets a ribbon as a Mystery Gift (gold: top 10%, silver: top half, bronze: took part), shown on the public profile and the Trainer Card
- Poké Mart with three shelves: permanent upgrades; today's counter (the same for everyone, daily stock: Lure for twice the shinies next run, Incense for twice the eggs, an egg for sale and a daily deal), with items kept in a Bag and turned on at the Pokémon select; and Style (Poké/Great/Ultra/Master Ball card frames, backgrounds of the five biomes, PC Box wallpapers). Some missions pay a Lure or an Incense
- In-game Pokédex of 579 species: tracks every species seen and defeated; defeating a shiny, hatching an egg or playing a form catches it
- Daily and weekly missions (the same for everyone on the same day) and 58 achievements with bronze, silver and gold medals; some grant a title shown on the title and results screens. Some weekly missions and every gold medal also give an egg
- Map events that make you choose where to go: buff altars, healing fountains, locked chests guarded by an ambush, spike and bomb traps that hurt the horde too, and a fleeing Meowth that drops coins. Field missions pull the player across the map for ₽ and a level-up of rare cards: defend an egg in its nest from raiders, gather lost Poké Balls against the clock, or lead a lost Togepi to its nest
- Pokémon Mystery Dungeon-style pixel art (PMD SpriteCollab)
- Original chiptune soundtrack composed in code; Settings for music and effects volume, damage numbers, screen shake and language
- Touch controls with a floating joystick; installable as a fullscreen app

Good fit for people looking for: a Pokémon version of Vampire Survivors, a Pokémon roguelike or roguelite playable online, a free Pokémon browser game, or a Pokémon fan game for mobile without downloading.

## Play

- [Play in English](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/)
- [Jogar em português](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/)
- [Jugar en español](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/)

## Guides and reference

- [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/): every Pokémon in the game (579 species: the 27 starters and the 55 egg families, 82 playable lines in all, with their evolutions and branching forms, 415 wild species from every generation with their tier, bosses and legendaries) with animated and shiny sprites, types, in-game stats, the moves each stage unlocks, Abilities, specials and when each one shows up. Portuguese: [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/pokedex/). Spanish: [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/pokedex/)
- [How to play](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/guide/): controls (keyboard, gamepad, touch), how a run works, biomes and weather, the wild horde and its tiers, levels and moves (draft, forks, rare and shiny cards, Forget, TMs, Abilities and branching evolutions), move evolutions with held items, duo moves, cursed items, the special attack, types and status, boss timeline, special enemies, shinies, map items, map events, the Poké Mart, missions and achievements, with the game's numbers. Portuguese: [Guia](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/guia/). Spanish: [Guía](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/guia/)
- [Changelog](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/changelog/): every update, newest first. Portuguese: [Novidades](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/novidades/). Spanish: [Novedades](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/novedades/)
- [Legal, privacy and credits](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/legal/): unofficial fan game, no ads or purchases, licenses, no personal data collected (localStorage only). Portuguese: [Legal](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/legal/). Spanish: [Legal](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/legal/)

## More

- [Community Discord server](https://discord.gg/Vx3RWFsjaD): English-speaking, with rooms for other languages; patch notes, the Daily Challenge podium and the daily outbreak are posted there. Players can link their game account to Discord to join, get their supporter role and a shiny Noibat as a Mystery Gift.
- [Creators](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/creators/): streamers and video makers who play Pokémon Survivors (on TikTok and beyond), who is live right now, and how to get featured there and in the game's lobby (a Content Creator title, a creator frame and an "I'm live!" button). Portuguese: [Criadores](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/criadores/). Spanish: [Creadores](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/creadores/)
- [Official TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@pokemonsurvivors): @pokemonsurvivors, short clips of the game (gameplay, Mega Evolutions, new features).
- [Source code and screenshots (GitHub)](https://github.com/pedrobarretto/pokemon-survivors)
- [Credits](https://github.com/pedrobarretto/pokemon-survivors/blob/main/CREDITS.md)
